prompt:
Game map background for a 2D top-down RPG, 1536x1024 landscape (3:2), filling the whole frame edge to edge, no border.

CAMERA: high-angle bird's-eye view looking down at about 50 degrees, orthographic-looking like a classic JRPG / Stardew-style town map: NO vanishing point, NO perspective convergence, all vertical building edges parallel and pointing straight up the image, ground plane seen almost from above. Building fronts are visible as short facades along the top and side edges; we see their roofs foreshortened. Consistent scale: a doorway is about 60 px wide and 100 px tall, a person would be about 90 px tall (but draw NO people).

STYLE: hand-painted cartoon illustration in exactly the painting style of the attached reference map (clean dark ink outlines on every shape, soft painterly cel shading, natural proportions, rich but slightly muted colours, no chibi, no pixel art, no 3D render, no photo). Mood and palette from the attached stage backdrop: Cyberpunk underground city in the year 2086, night-blue shadows, rusty metal, corrugated sheet metal, cables, steam, wet ground with reflections, neon light in hot pink, cyan and violet, warm yellow window light as accent. Readable game art: the walkable ground is large, flat, clearly lit and uncluttered; props sit at the edges; strong value contrast between floor (walkable) and walls/props (blocking).

The attached images are references for painting style, camera angle, scale and colour ONLY. Do not copy their buildings or layout and do not draw any characters.

STRICT: no people, no figures, no animals, no silhouettes of persons, no readable text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no watermarks, no signature, no frame, no UI.

LOCATION: Follow the layout of the attached grey blockout sketch: light = walkable ground, dark = buildings/blocking, cyan = exits. The last attached image is only the floor-plan sketch, not its look (ignore its labels, they are not part of the picture). "Funkturm-Ruine", a lonely ruined radio station on a rocky outcrop in the desert wasteland, seen from above. The large walkable area is a wide flat yard of packed ochre sand and gravel filling the middle and the whole lower half of the image, open and uncluttered, with a sandy dirt track coming in from the bottom edge.
TOP LEFT TO TOP CENTER: a steep reddish rock cliff forms the back of the scene. Built into its foot: a half-buried concrete bunker with a heavy steel door facing south onto the yard; on the bunker roof grows a dense forest of antennas, satellite dishes, aerials and wires; thick cables hang down from the rocks like jungle lianas (drawn thin so they don't hide the floor). 
In front of the bunker door, CENTER-RIGHT of it: the most eye-catching spot - an open-air radio studio under a patched canvas awning: a big old mixing desk with knobs and faders, two microphones on stands, a reel-to-reel tape machine, a red "on air" lamp (a lamp, no letters), a worn armchair.
CENTER-LEFT in front of the bunker: a record archive - wooden shelves and crates stuffed with vinyl records under a corrugated metal roof.
LEFT SIDE: a tall old wind turbine on a lattice mast with colourful fabric ribbons fluttering from its blades, a tool box and spare parts at its base; high up near its hub a messy nest of scrap and wires (a drone nest).
TOP RIGHT: a raised flat rock plateau, reachable by a winding rocky path going up from the yard on the right; on the plateau lies a huge toppled, bent steel transmission mast, its red-white lattice snapped and bent over the edge.
CENTER-RIGHT of the yard: a long clothes line between two poles with dozens of black vinyl records hanging on pegs to dry, glinting in the sun.
BOTTOM LEFT: an old rusty camper van with a sun awning and a satellite dish, a couple of plastic chairs, cacti.
BOTTOM RIGHT: a pile of scrap metal, old speakers and broken radio cabinets.
Small things at the edges: rocks, dry bushes, cable drums, a solar panel, oil barrels.
EXITS clearly readable at the image edges: BOTTOM edge (south), center - the sandy track leaves the image toward the desert road.
Light and material: wasteland in warm late-afternoon daylight, dusty orange sand and reddish rocks, dry ground without puddles, long soft shadows; small warm lamp lights on the radio desk.
